reference: In the small coastal town of Marlow Bay, a problem that began far away gradually became impossible to ignore. For years, residents had noticed that the tide seemed to bring more plastic than fish. The town council, led by Mayor Elena Ruiz, first responded by organizing monthly beach clean-ups. These were popular, but they did not address the source of the waste. Meanwhile, a group of local fishermen, including Tomás Herrera, reported that their nets were catching fewer fish and more debris. They argued that the problem was not just local; it was regional, because currents carried rubbish from neighboring countries.
